discussion_comments.comment_body:
*medium*

`.then(attach, onError)` catches a rejected spawn but not an exception thrown inside `attach` itself (stream setup, the Bun socket check). That becomes an unhandled rejection and the synthetic child never fails or closes, so the command can sit until the outer timeout. `.then(attach).catch(fail)` covers both.

*medium*

`MxcProcess.kill()` calls `throwIfFailed(this.native.kill(...))`, so it throws on a non-zero status. `SandboxedProcess.kill` doesn't catch, and the caller in `bash.ts` ignores the promise from `killProcessTree().finally(...)`, so a failed kill becomes an unhandled rejection in the CLI or extension host and can terminate it depending on the runtime's unhandled-rejection setting. Wrap it and route the error through `fail`.

[P2] Do not unconditionally make timeouts eligible for whole-turn retry. A TimeoutError means the client stopped waiting; it does not establish that the provider failure is transient or that the request was not processed. This override also bypasses the existing stream-phase and exhausted-SDK-budget checks. With the new 120-second limit and three agent retries, a silent hosted provider can consume about eight minutes before failing. Please remove this blanket override and the unconditional timeout return in isRetryableProviderError, retaining the timeout limits and diagnostics. Add coverage showing that a native timeout alone does not grant a new whole-turn retry budget and that existing SDK retryability/budget decisions remain respected.
why don't we want a retry here?

Valid. `hub-websocket-server.ts` answers every HTTP request with `503 Starting` between `listen()` and `published = true`, and `probeHubServer` maps any non-OK response to `invalid-response`, which `probeHubForStartup` turns into a throw. The post-spawn loop only swallows `HubStartupProbeTimeoutError`, so if a poll lands in that window the whole `ensureDetachedHubServer` fails. Confirmed against a server that returns `503 Starting`: `probeHubForStartup` throws "The existing Hub endpoint returned an invalid health response".

Before this PR `!response.ok` returned `undefined` (treated as not a hub, never fatal). Suggest restoring that for `invalid-response` in `probeHubForStartup` (return `undefined`), and either keep polling on 503 specifically or add a `"starting"` status for it so the loop waits for publication like it does for `timeout`.

Valid. Fixed in 9081097ad3: the queue now holds the `structuredClone` snapshot, so the worker gets the args as they were at call time, and a clone error still rejects at call time. On flush, calls that already timed out are skipped, and a `postMessage` failure rejects that call instead of throwing from the message listener.

New `worker-sandbox.test.ts` uses a bootstrap that delays `ready`. It covers changing args (and adding a function) after the call, rejecting an uncloneable call, and a call timing out before ready. Run against the previous code, the args test reproduces this report: an unhandled `DataCloneError` and a hung call.

discussion_comments.comment_body: Agreed the bare log was too quiet, but settling `run()` here would be wrong: a hook is free to ignore its input, and one that exits 0 without reading must still count as success (added a test for exactly that). The still-alive case is also mostly theoretical on Unix, since hooks run through `sh -c` and the shell holds the pipe's read end open for the script's lifetime, so closing stdin inside the script never produces an EPIPE; the write only fails once the whole hook process tree is gone, and `close` follows right after. What I changed: the stdin failure is now recorded and appended to the timeout and non-zero-exit errors ("...The hook stopped reading its input before it was fully delivered (write EPIPE)."), and the exit-code test asserts it.

Valid, and introduced by the previous revision. Fixed by killing the child when its stdin write fails: the connection is dead at that point regardless, and the exit handler then fails the pending requests at once. A server that already exited keeps its real exit status, so the exit-code report Dom asked for is unchanged. Added a test with a server that closes stdin but stays alive; it rejects within milliseconds rather than at the request timeout.
Fixed: the batch is requeued and the retry scheduled before `onError` runs, and `onError` is wrapped so a throwing logger can't escape.

Fixed — the outcome is now classified by a `loopAcceptsTurn` helper mirroring the loop's full decision chain: aborted throws, no renderable output is rejected as empty, and an errored or re-truncated retry counts as recovered only when it produced tool calls the loop will execute. (The suggested predicate had one hole — an `aborted` finish with tool calls would have recorded success on a run the loop aborts — which the helper closes.) Covered by a new test: retry errors mid-stream after a tool call, the loop executes it, the task completes, telemetry records succeeded.
[P2] A transient stream failure drops already-executed model tools and their results from conversation history.

Fixed in 5981f96cb0. Recorded model-tool calls and received results are saved before failing; errors stay errors and missing results remain unknown. Unfinished local calls never execute. Added history/resume regression tests.

Fixed in d862eca164. Unknown-finish recovery now resets only after a successful tool result. Turns containing only malformed, missing, or failed tool calls count toward the two-continuation limit, and their tool error results are retained before failure. Added regression tests for all three cases and successful tool progress.

Valid — and together with the afterModel finding below, this made the pattern undeniable: five windows of the same class means the design is wrong, not the placement. Recording the reason on every finish event and chasing failure windows with resets cannot terminate, because any callback that throws between a finish and the next reset inherits stale state.

So I inverted it rather than patch a sixth window. Nothing is recorded on finish events anymore; the reason is set immediately before each finish-reason-driven throw (empty turn, max-tokens with no tool calls, provider error with no tool calls). Nothing can interleave between a synchronous set-and-throw and the run-level catch, so `sdk.error` can never pick up a reason from a request that did not cause the failure — this window, the afterModel one, and any future callback-throw site are all closed by construction. Both reset sites are deleted; net less state juggling than before.

Regression tests added for both new windows (each verified to fail on the reset-based design); the four earlier stale-attribution tests now pin the property under the new mechanism. Agents suite 76/76.

Valid, and fixed in b6807e2ab. When `createCheckpoint` throws, the hook records a failure for that run, then rethrows, so the existing error behavior is unchanged. Recording is best effort, so a failed metadata write can't replace the original error. Covered by `records a failure, then rethrows, when a custom checkpoint throws` in `checkpoint-hooks.test.ts`.

On store failure this sends the full result and skips the aggregate budget. Reproduced: 500k chars against a 1,000-byte budget went to the provider as-is. Today that request is truncated and succeeds; here it fails every turn.

Updated: 

- Results are saved and shortened once; history retains the preview and path.
- Save failures log a warning and keep truncated output without failing the tool.
- Aggregate budgeting still applies without restoring oversized results.

Fixed in 9338bc95a5. The viewer's transcript and status reads now wait for the hub link (new `HubLink.connected(withinMs)`, up to 5 s) instead of failing at once while it connects, so a new or forked chat's first viewer is served a set. A read the link drops is retried once after the link is back; a hub error reply still counts as an answer, and no running hub or a disposed link answers immediately. A failed read now returns "unknown" rather than an empty transcript.
